grand_strategy.reading: Malta sells a flag, a licence and a harbour, and its grand strategy is to keep the EU's structure around those sales while refusing to be a military ally. Neutrality makes it useful as a host of talks and a Chair of the OSCE, and gives it a reason to stay out of the EU defence money; the Libyan maritime file and the Italian energy link matter more to it than any great power. The 2025 CJEU ruling on citizenship and the shadow-fleet reputation problem show the price of selling instruments of the state. Malta recognised Palestine on 22 September 2025 (recorded in the recognition dataset, not repeated here), a stance that sits with the EU line rather than against it.

stances.note: Italy is the neighbour with the power and gas links (a second electricity cable parallel to the Ragusa interconnector, the Delimara-Gela pipeline at tender). Transactional, no treaty found in the sources. Bond none: no kinship or grievance in the sources. No source uses the word partner for Italy; our reading of the structure (C). Migration coordination with Italy is not evidenced by a source we could read, so it is not claimed here.

stances.note: Cooperates on migration and border management out of necessity (the 2020 memorandum, the 2025-26 security contacts in Tripoli) while contesting the maritime limits: Tripoli's unilateral claim to lodge its outer limits with the UN, which Malta protested. Talks agreed on 10 Sep 2025 (year inferred from the article). The 2020 memorandum was for three years; renewal not found. Bond none. The 1984 treaty of friendship with Gaddafi is an old link (Wikipedia index, not used as a source).

stances.note: Full member bound by EU law and sanctions, aligned on the single market and Russia sanctions. The friction is visible: the CJEU ruling of 29 Apr 2025 against the citizenship scheme; Malta stays out of EU defence money in the constitutional terms of its neutrality (State Advocate: the conclusions adequately safeguard neutrality). Accession date (1 May 2004) is the standard date, not in the sources we read. Bond affinity: a member of the club, not kin.

stances_toward.note: Malta signed the 2020 migration memorandum with Tripoli (two coordination centres, one in Tripoli and one in Valletta) and agreed talks on the maritime border in September 2025, after protesting Tripoli's unilateral move to lodge its outer limits with the UN. Malta's interior minister was among those expelled from Benghazi with the EU commissioner on 8 Jul 2025, so Valletta pays attention to both halves. Malta's own stance toward Libya is reluctant_partner; from Tripoli's side the same file reads as ordinary partnership: cooperation on migration with a live boundary dispute that talks, not force, will settle. Bond - none.

relations_from.summary: Malta partly relies on electricity imported from Italy; a second 200 MW cable parallel to the Ragusa interconnector was targeted for completion in 2025. No completion was confirmed in the sources.

Melita TransGas plans a 159 km gas pipeline from Delimara to Gela (Sicily), hydrogen-ready, with an initial flow from Italy to Malta of up to 1.2 bcm a year; it is to replace the LNG floating unit at Delimara. Still at tender and not built, per the sources; the cost is quoted at USD 400m (trade.gov) or EUR 350-400m (other sources).
